verdict: Do not ship as judged; the remaining work is small and was done in r5.

usability.finding: The round-3 blocker was still open. At seven siblings — the true product maximum, since family.ts offers none above MAX_FAMILY_OFFER — the landscape frame is pixel-identical to the five-sibling one except for a digit in the button. Three children have zero pixels on the glass and the button says 'Check in all 8'. A parent cannot tell 6 from 8 on this screen, and the kiosk has no undo.
usability.note: The CSS carried a fully specified `.more` rule — brand-300, left-aligned, under the list — and the builder never emitted the element. grep found 0 occurrences of class="more" across all eight pages. The rule was decoration on a selector that never matched.

usability.finding: The overflow signal was gated on `siblings.length > 4`, a hand-written number, and it was already off by one: the list clips at four. So a five-child family got a silent truncation with no fade, no count and no scrollbar. Same failure mode as the class rename one level up — a rule that is right until the thing it is guessing about changes.

The ask was still 18px. `.whoelse .ask` outranked the element-scoped `.ask` on specificity, so r4's restoration was inert in exactly the quiet way the rename had been. The note said 20px; the pixels said 18.

design.finding: The fade was a fixed 32px scrim from the list's bottom edge, and the edge landed wherever the arithmetic left it — through a row's contents. A ticked child rendered as the most receded object on the glass: half-ink name, dimmed chip, in the one column a parent scans for state. 'A row is either printed or hidden; half a ticked child at half value is the one state this screen cannot render.'

A fixed band centred by the flex parent anchors *both* ends, not the one the note claimed. On the portrait kiosk that scrolled a list it had room to print — 528px of unused page while a child was clipped. At full page the portrait column holds ten rows and the maximum is seven, so that orientation never needs a scroller at all.
51.25rem is 820px and the landscape glass is 800, so the band mechanism did not exist there: the stack pooled at the bottom with a 9:1 asymmetry against 2:1 on portrait.

The display line was set solid and filled 94% of the track it now owns, so the first name a character longer wrapped with descenders landing in the caps below — on the one element the parent is there to verify.

confirmed_working: The clear band above the commit is 48px in all four scenes at both viewports, and the commit occupies an identical y in every scene. 'This invariant is now the best-behaved thing on the screen.'
The measure is fixed: 448 portrait, 576 landscape, identical across scenes. The child's name no longer sizes the commit.

Four type sizes, three weights, and the ink ramp reads as levels: 8 within the list, 14 within the identity, 16 caption-to-list, 37 identity-to-region, 48 region-to-commit, 72 commit-to-exit — monotonic with semantic distance.
The conditional fade left `family` and `added` drawing solid rows with intact edges and full-white ticks.
The antecedent fix holds; 'Another child' can no longer be read as 'not this child'.
fixed_in_r5: The count is emitted and measured — rows counted, not pixels divided — and it is revealed before the list is measured, because it takes its own height out of the region.
The list's height is quantised to the row pitch, so the scroll edge always falls in the 8px between cards and never through a name.
The scrim is gone. A mask says 'more' by taking legibility away, which is a strange way to say a child exists below the line; the count says it positively instead.
Only the bottom is anchored: full height with the commit a constant distance up from the bezel, top free to rise. The portrait kiosk now prints all seven without scrolling.
The ask's losing declaration deleted rather than a third added.
The display line has leading that survives a second line.
